summary:
The repeated probe executed with a valid predicate and both comparisons hold in all 25 rounds, so the last open question is now closed with a measured interpretation, a fact, and an explicitly retained unexplained observation (valid:true).

Receipt 38d727906cc1458b9dfdcd9e337fc5a2 (completed, exit 0) parsed 200 events: 25 per-round admissions, 75 per-node start events, 75 per-node results and 25 round results. Both comparisons hold with every round evaluated and no diagnostics — comparison 0 (all_converged true) and comparison 1 (any_lag_with_entry false) each evaluated the round results at indices 7, 15, 23 … 199. Per-round maximum wait was 0–6ms with median 0, and all 75 node results reported the joining voter visible with the configuration entry present in the log store. The operands also show an expected asymmetry rather than the lag the question asked about: one final-round node published the three-server membership while its committed configuration index was still behind, because appending a configuration entry updates the published latest configuration (processConfigurationLogEntry → setLatestConfiguration, which also writes the atomic copy that GetConfiguration returns) while the committed configuration advances only when the leader's commit index reaches it.

The question is marked explained with its boundaries: answered only for the reproduced scenario shape over the in-memory transport, reading published content and the log store at the end of each window; the earlier probe for this question is explicitly superseded because its predicate was the configuration index accessor that returns a constant zero; and the earlier local failure of the captured TestRaft_ProtocolVersion_Upgrade_2_3 (peer mismatch in roughly two of three isolated runs) remains unexplained and is not attributed — under instrumentation the same scenario converges in milliseconds. A fact was promoted with executions at indices 7, 15, 23, 191 and 199, and the interpretation carries Chinese report fields summarising the result for offline review.
